title: Affine pushforward detects degree-zero concentration
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be an affine morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and let $E$ be an object of $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(X)$ [def-pc-derived-category]. Then $E$ is represented by a quasi-coherent sheaf in degree zero if and only if $Rf_*E$ [def-pc-derived-direct-image] is represented by a quasi-coherent sheaf in degree zero; in that case the degree-zero sheaf is $f_*E$.

source.place: Tag 0AVW, lemma-affine-morphism-equivalence; Tag 08I8, lemma-affine-morphism (Rf_* reflects isomorphisms on D_QCoh for f affine); Cohomology of Schemes Tag 01XC, coherent-lemma-relative-affine-vanishing (R^if_*F = 0 for i>0, F quasi-coherent, f affine)

proof.text: Use lem-sc-affine-derived-pushforward-t-exact to obtain preservation of quasi-coherent cohomology and the equivalences of both standard bounds at zero. An isomorphism E ≅ F[0] gives both bounds on E by Mathlib singleFunctor instances and isomorphism invariance. Transfer them to Rf_*E and apply DerivedCategory.exists_iso_singleFunctor_obj_of_isGE_of_isLE. For its representing module G, map the representation isomorphism under H^0 and compose with singleFunctorCompHomologyFunctorIso to obtain H^0(Rf_*E) ≅ G. Transport quasi-coherence along this isomorphism.

Conversely, an isomorphism Rf_*E ≅ G[0] gives both bounds on Rf_*E. Reflect them using lem-sc-affine-derived-pushforward-t-exact and apply the same Mathlib representation lemma to E. Its representing module F is quasi-coherent because H^0(E) ≅ F, by mapping the representation isomorphism under H^0 and composing with singleFunctorCompHomologyFunctorIso.

For a representing module F and e : E ≅ F[0], use lem-sc-affine-derived-cohomology at i = 0 to obtain H^0(Rf_*E) ≅ f_*H^0(E). Compose the image under ordinary f_* of H^0(e) followed by singleFunctorCompHomologyFunctorIso to obtain H^0(Rf_*E) ≅ f_*F.
